name: Corona Borealis
introduction: is the Northern Crown, a small, graceful semicircle of stars between Boötes and Hercules. In Greek myth, it is the crown that Dionysus gave to Ariadne. It is best seen on northern spring and summer evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Corona Borealis is famous for unusual variable stars. T Coronae Borealis, the Blaze Star, is a recurrent nova: a white dwarf that gathers gas from a red giant companion until it ignites in a thermonuclear explosion, roughly every 80 years. It flared in 1866 and 1946, briefly becoming as bright as Polaris.
R Coronae Borealis does the opposite: it occasionally fades by thousands of times when clouds of soot condense around it, then slowly reappears.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alphecca](hip:76267), also called Gemma, the jewel of the crown, is an eclipsing binary 77 light-years away. [Nusakan](hip:75695) is a star with a strong magnetic field and an unusual chemical composition.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Far beyond the stars lies the Corona Borealis Supercluster, a dense concentration of galaxy clusters about a billion light-years away. Some astronomers have even proposed a much larger structure in this direction, the Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall.
